summary: Five-part It Could Happen Here series by Steven Monacelli tracing the 2025 West Texas measles outbreak back through US anti-vaccine history, faith-healing Christianity, eugenic thinking and RFK Jr.'s rise to run federal health policy.

evidence.note: Introduced as a compilation of the week's It Could Happen Here episodes
Outbreak began in Gaines County, Texas in January 2025 and spread to other states
UK compulsory vaccination laws and riots from 1853, leading to the 1898 exemption
Historian on Sims's experiments on enslaved women and the Tuskegee study as roots of distrust
Children's Health Defense founded 2007, pushes homeopathy and Great Reset conspiracy
2014-15 California outbreak and exemption ban set off red-state health freedom backlash
Garrison recounts an unvaccinated childhood in a Texas-linked church in Saskatchewan
Kenneth Copeland: 2013 measles outbreak at his daughter's church and COVID-era preaching
Fort Worth Christian school celebrates being least vaccinated in Texas
Galton coins eugenics in 1883; early eugenicists feared vaccines saved the unfit
Great Barrington Declaration framed as soft eugenics, linked to MAHA
Final episode projects the return of polio and other diseases under current policy

notes: Format crossover: a compilation of an It Could Happen Here miniseries hosted by Steven Monacelli, so roles empty (primary is a movement). Covered span starts at 1853 British anti-vaccination resistance; Jenner 1796 is background. GB history is about a minute, so left out of setting. Transcript spells the Lubbock director Catherine Wells; Katherine Wells is the usual spelling. Interviewees listed as guests.
